cs.t: I use a 2.5 year old BlackBerry Key2 LE. I'm hoping this one's charging port doesn't break like my previous KeyOne which gave out around the 2 year mark. I prefer the static keyboard style of the Key line over the slide-out ones popular with early Android devices such as the Droid line.
cs.th: Ask HN: Is anyone using a phone with a physical keyboard?

cs.t: Look into the BlackBerry Classic, which was released in late 2014 or early 2015 and runs BB10. It's discontinued, but you should be able to find it on ebay for much cheaper than a new KeyOne/Key2 (which are quite large compared to the Classic). It has a great keyboard and all the built-in stuff works very well and is easy to use (SMS, phone, camera, calculator, calendar, notes, music player, maps, etc.). Battery life is pretty good too, or at least it was when new. I used this phone until the end of 2017, at which point the outdated browser and dead app store (free apps only) started to seriously limit its functionality, but if you don't need those it would work just fine. I use a KeyOne now, but I miss the Classic's smaller form factor.
cs.th: Ask HN: What is the best “dumb” phone?

cs.t: I gave up on the whole mess and bought a BlackBerry KeyOne, later replaced by a Key2, on which I have disabled all the autocomplete/suggestion stuff. It's quicker, simpler, I get what I want, my mistakes are my own and not the phone's, and I no longer hate using phones.
cs.th: Ask HN: Physical keyboards vs. on-screen keyboards, what do I do wrong?
